note_claims.claim: Head injury after a mechanical fall at home at about 07:45.
Tripped on a rug and struck the left side of her head on a door frame.
Patient reports feeling muddled for about 10 minutes afterwards.
Loss of consciousness uncertain (unwitnessed).
No vomiting.
Mild headache at the impact site.
No visual disturbance, limb weakness or neck pain.
No preceding dizziness or presyncope.
Last apixaban dose this morning, after the fall.
Tetanus up to date.
Apixaban 2.5 mg twice daily (atrial fibrillation).
Bisoprolol 2.5 mg once daily.
Amlodipine 5 mg once daily.
Allergic to penicillin (swelling).
Glasgow Coma Score is 15.
3 cm laceration with haematoma over the left temple.
Pupils are equal and reactive.
Normal power in all limbs.
No cervical spine midline tenderness.
Heart rate is irregular at about 80.
Blood pressure is 146 over 82.
CT head (anticoagulated) is required to check for internal bleeding.
Wound cleaned and closed with steri-strips.
Discharge with daughter, who will stay with her for 24 hours if CT is normal.
Call 999 or return immediately if patient becomes drowsy, confused, vomits again, has a worsening headache, a fit, or any weakness.
Written head injury advice given to daughter.

transcript_facts.fact: Clinician is Dr Pemberton.
Relative is the patient's daughter, Sue.
Clinician asks the patient what happened.
Patient tripped on the rug in the hall and banged her head on the door frame.
Patient reports the time of the fall was about half past nine.
Relative corrects the time, stating it was about quarter to eight, noting the post hadn't come and the patient hadn't had breakfast.
Patient acknowledges the relative's correction.
Patient states the injury was on the left side, by their eye.
Patient states they do not think they blacked out.
Relative states that when she arrived about ten minutes later, the patient was muddled and kept asking what day it was, lasting maybe ten minutes.
Patient does not remember Sue arriving.
Relative states the patient was sick once in the car on the way to the hospital.
Patient does not remember being sick in the car.
Patient reports a bit of a headache where they hit the head.
Patient denies problems with vision, weakness in arms or legs.
Patient denies neck pain.
Patient states they caught their foot on the rug and were not dizzy.
Relative states the patient is on Apixaban 2.5 mg twice a day for heart rhythm, Bisoprolol 2.5 mg once a day, and Amlodipine 5 mg once daily.
Patient states they last took Apixaban this morning with breakfast, after the fall.
Patient reports an allergy to penicillin, which causes swelling.
Clinician notes the patient's Glasgow Coma Score is 15.
Clinician notes there is a cut about 3 centimetres long on the left temple with a bump around it.
Clinician notes the patient's pupils are equal and reactive to light.
Clinician notes strength is normal everywhere.
Clinician notes the patient's heart rate is irregular at about 80 and blood pressure is 146 over 82.
Clinician plans a CT scan of the head to check for internal bleeding because the patient is on a blood thinner.
Clinician plans to hold off the evening dose of Apixaban until the scan is seen.
Clinician plans to clean and close the cut with steri-strips.
Patient confirms they are up to date with tetanus.
Clinician states that if the scan is normal, the patient can go home with Sue, who will stay with her for 24 hours.
Clinician provides safety-netting instructions: call 999 or return immediately if the patient becomes drowsy, confused, vomits again, has a worsening headache, a fit, or any weakness.
